note: 'And this is the interpretation of the message: MENE means that God has numbered the days of your reign and brought it to an end.' (Dan 5:26).
'This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.' (Dan 2:36).
'Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.' (Dan 8:16).

**He does not interpret it -- he overhears the interpretation.** An enemy soldier tells the dream and his fellow reads it: 'This is nothing less than the sword of Gideon' (Judg 7:14). Gideon worships and goes (7:15). It is the only dream in the corpus whose key is supplied by the people it is against.
'Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?' (Gen 37:10) -- **the key given by the man rebuking it.**
'Listen to this dream I had' (Gen 37:6).; Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.
'Then Joseph had another dream and told it to his brothers' (Gen 37:9).
The words of the writing seen at Daniel 5:5.
'the large horn between his eyes is the first king' (Dan 8:21).
The key to the vision at Daniel 8:3.
'the seven lampstands are the seven churches' (Rev 1:20).
The key to the vision at Revelation 1:12.
'The secret which the king has demanded can’t be shown to the king by wise men' (Dan 2:27).
'no one could interpret them for him' (Gen 41:8), and Joseph's disclaimer at 41:16.
'All the wise men thereof' (Gen 41:8); 'No wise man ... can explain to the king' (Dan 2:27). **In both scenes the professionals of wisdom are the ones who fail.**
'four great beasts came up out of the sea' (Dan 7:3).
'The first beast was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle' (Dan 7:4).
The key to the four beasts of Daniel 7:3.
The key to the image seen at Daniel 2:31.
'a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue' (Dan 2:34), read as a kingdom at 2:44.
'You are that head of gold.' (Dan 2:38) -- **stated, and of a named living man.**
